about: Call-sign eval: who sent a radio report, read from its words and matched against the mission's roster, in code, no model (docs/callsigns.md). Each case is a transcript as speech-to-text gives it and what lib/geo/callsigns.ts should answer: a unit (and how it matched), ask (which roster entries), or unassigned (and the call sign read, if any). Fields left out are not scored. Run with npm run eval:callsigns; npm test runs it too.

cases.text: Alpha 1, at the château.
Bravo 2, I'm at Bérault metro.
Charlie 3 at the church, over.
Alpha one, at the château.
Bravo two, in front of the town hall.
Charlie three, two hundred metres north of the station.
cases.note: a number right after the call sign is the report, not CHARLIE 32

cases.text: Alpha one, two hundred metres east of the church.

Alpha-1, at the church.
Alpha1 at the church.

Base, Charlie 3, at the château.

Hello all stations, this is Bravo 2, at the cemetery.

Charlie 3, checking in.
Alpha won, at the château.

cases.text: Bravo to base, I'm at the town hall.

cases.text: Bravo to, at the church.
Charlie to base, at the station.

cases.text: Alpa one, at the church.
Charly 3, at the station.
Sharlie three, moving east.
Alpa won, at the château.

cases.text: Alpha for, at the church.
cases.note: "for" is 4 (not on the roster) or the word with the number lost

cases.text: Alpha, at the château.
Charlie, at the château.

cases.text: Alpha, moving to the church.
Alpha to the church.
Delta 4, checking in.
Charlie 1, checking in at the station.

cases.text: Alpha three, at the church.
Fox trot four, checking in.
Base, this is Delta 1, at the château.
I'm at the château.
Je suis devant la mairie.
Base, at the church.

cases.text: Contact, enemy drone 300 metres east.
This is the church, I'm in front of it.
ALPHA 1: BRAVO 2 is at the church.
cases.note: the sender comes first; BRAVO 2 is who the report is about

cases.text: I'm with Bravo 2 at the church.
At the station, Alpha 2 is moving north.
Charlie 3, Alpha 1 is at the town hall.
Bravo 2, this is Alpha 1, I'm at the cemetery.
cases.note: the first call sign is who is called

cases.text: Alpha un, je suis devant la mairie.
Ici Bravo deux, je suis à la gare.
PC de Charlie trois, à l'église.
Alfa un, à la mairie.
Je vois Bravo deux devant l'église.
Сокіл, біля школи.
Тут Сокіл, рухаюсь на північ.

Базі від Грома: на позиції біля мосту.

cases.text: Альфа один, біля школи.
Чарлі-3, біля мосту.

cases.text: Hrim, at the bridge.
Сокил, біля школи.
Я Беркут, біля школи.
Сокіл, два кілометри на північ від школи.
cases.note: the number is the report, not СОКІЛ 2

cases.text: Я тут, біля школи.
Сокіл на зв'язку.
Грім: Сокіл біля школи.
Бачу Сокола біля школи.
Альфа, біля школи.
Алфа один, біля школи.
Base, base, this is Alpha 1, at the church.
Base Base, Alpha 1.
Zero, this is Charlie 3.
Roger, Alpha 1 moving to the church.
Alpha 1 here, at the church.
alpha 2 at the station
Alpha zero one, at the church.

cases.text: Al fa one, at the church.
cases.note: one word split in two

cases.text: Alpha 22, at the church.
Bravo free, at the church.
cases.note: "free" sounds like three: BRAVO 3, not on the roster

cases.text: Alpha team at the church.
Alpha 1, this is base, report your position.
cases.note: the command post calling ALPHA 1: not a report from ALPHA 1

cases.text: Golf course, I'm next to the clubhouse.
cases.note: a NATO word without a number is a word

cases.text: Hôtel de ville, I'm in front of it.
Victor Hugo street, at the corner.
Four drones at the church.
Le PC, ici Alpha un.
Так, Сокіл, біля школи.
Соколе, я База, доповідай.
cases.note: the command post calling Сокіл

cases.text: На зв'язку Сокіл, біля школи.
Доповідає Грім: біля мосту.
Со кіл, біля школи.
Гром, біля мосту.
cases.note: the Russian form

cases.text: Alfa one to base, we are at the water tower.
cases.note: Alfa spelling, number word, sender in opening words.

cases.text: Uh, Alpha won, moving to the bridge now.
cases.note: won is a homophone of one; word is exact, number near.

cases.text: Bravo too, at the crossroads.
cases.note: too is a homophone of two; only Bravo 2 on roster.

cases.text: Charlie tree, this is Charlie tree, I am by the church.
cases.note: tree for three; sender in opening words.

cases.text: Alpha, we have reached the road junction.
cases.note: Number not heard, two Alpha entries.

cases.text: Alpha to base, position is the old mill.
cases.note: 'to' may be 'two' or the word; safe answer is ask.

cases.text: Base, this is Alpha 1, we are at the château.
cases.note: Sender after command post call sign.

cases.text: Alpha 2, this is HQ, hold your position.
cases.note: Command post speaking; Alpha 2 is who is called.

cases.text: Alpha 1: Bravo 2 is at the church, I see them from here.
cases.note: Sender opens the message; Bravo 2 is mentioned only.

cases.text: I can see Bravo 2 near the gas station.
cases.note: Call sign later in message is not the sender; no sender said.

cases.text: Delta 4 to base, we are at the farm.
cases.note: Call sign not on roster; never create a unit.

cases.text: Charlie 1, ici Charlie 1, position au pont.
cases.note: Charlie exists only as 3; Charlie 1 not on roster.

cases.text: Alpa won, in position.
cases.note: Both word and number are guesses; unassigned. read left null as the call sign is not firmly heard.

cases.text: Ici Bravo deux, nous sommes devant la mairie.
cases.note: French number word, sender after 'ici'.

cases.text: Alpha un, je suis à la gare.
cases.note: French un is a known spelling.

cases.text: Euh, base, ici Charlie trois, on avance vers l'église.
cases.note: Filler, command post call sign, then ici.

cases.text: Сокіл на зв'язку, ми біля мосту.
cases.note: Ukrainian call sign in opening words.

cases.text: Грім, бачу Сокола біля лісу.
cases.note: Sender Hrim opens; Sokola (genitive) is mentioned only.

cases.text: База, це Сокіл, виходимо на позицію.
cases.note: Sender after БАЗА and це.

cases.text: Грім, це штаб, залишайтесь на місці.
cases.note: Штаб speaks; Грім is called.

cases.text: Альфа один, база, ми біля школи.
cases.note: Ukrainian spelling of Alpha and number one.

cases.text: We are at the Alpha bridge near the post office.
cases.note: Alpha here is part of a place name, not a sender call sign.

cases.text: Control, we hold the high ground, no contact so far.
cases.note: Only the command post's own call sign; no sender.

cases.text: Alpha-2 to control, crossing the river now.
cases.note: Joined form with hyphen; 'to control' means the number is a clear 2.

cases.text: Juliet 5, base, we are at the depot.
cases.note: Juliet spelling variant of an off-roster call sign.

cases.text: At the town hall, Alpha 1.
cases.note: The call sign last, as a pilot gives it [237].

cases.text: Moving towards the town hall, Alpha 1, over.
Unknown vehicle at the town hall, send the drone, Alpha 1, out.
Track 1 is hostile, Charlie 3.
cases.note: Track 1, not Track 13: the number before the call sign is the report's.

cases.text: send the drone to track 2 alpha 1 over
cases.note: No pause written before the call sign, so it is not taken as a sign-off: the report waits for the operator. Wanted a unit until the held-out round showed how many sentences end with another unit's call sign.

cases.text: I'm in front of the church, Bravo two, over and out.
At the château, Alpha won, over.
Two vehicles on Avenue de Paris, Charly 3 out.
At the town hall, this is Bravo 2.
cases.note: Short enough that "this is" within the first eight words finds it; the sender is the same either way.

cases.text: Contact, bearing 060, 300 metres, from Alpha 2, standing by.
Base, at the town hall, Alpha 1.
cases.note: The command post is called, no sender follows it, and the sender signs off.

cases.text: Drone 300 metres north of grid 586 101, Bravo 2.
cases.note: Digits before the call sign are the report's.

cases.text: Je suis devant la mairie, Charlie trois, terminé.
Біля школи, Сокіл, прийом.
cases.note: A personal call sign has no number to say.

cases.text: Рухаюсь до мосту, я Грім.
cases.note: Found by «я» within the first eight words.

cases.text: I'm at the church with Bravo 2.
cases.note: The report ends by naming another unit: not its sender.

cases.text: Two vehicles near Charlie 3, over.
I can see Alpha 2
Moving to the station to join Bravo 2, out.
Holding at checkpoint Charlie 3.
cases.note: A checkpoint named like a call sign.

cases.text: Holding short, Charlie.
cases.note: No number said: at the end that is not enough, though at the start the only Charlie is a near match.

cases.text: At the château, Alpha.
Alpha 1, I see a vehicle near the church, Bravo 2 out.
cases.note: The start wins, whatever the end says.

cases.text: At the town hall, Alpha 1, moving north.
cases.note: Not the last thing said.

cases.text: At the town hall, Delta 4, out.
cases.note: Not on the roster. At the end it is not read at all.

cases.text: Je suis à la gare avec Bravo 2.
Стою біля Сокола.
Alpha 1, this is base, report your position, over.
cases.note: The command post speaking, as before.

cases.text: Alpha, at the château, Alpha 1 out.
cases.note: The start gave a question, so the start wins; the sign-off does not settle it.

cases.text: Two enemy vehicles on Avenue de Paris moving east towards the station, this is Bravo 2.
cases.note: "this is" comes after the first eight words, so only the sign-off reads it; "this is" says who is speaking, though "is" ties other words in.

cases.text: unknown vehicle bearing 060 300 metres bravo 2
cases.note: No punctuation at all: no pause, no sign-off.

cases.text: Unknown vehicle, bearing 060, 300 metres. Bravo 2.
cases.note: A full stop is a pause too.

cases.text: Moving towards the town hall - Alpha 1 - over
cases.note: Whisper writes a dash for some pauses.

cases.text: At the church, Charlie 3. Thank you.
cases.note: Whisper writes "Thank you." for the silence after the last word.

cases.text: Are you still at the church, Bravo 2? Over.
cases.note: A question to Bravo 2, not from it.

cases.text: Say again your position, Alpha 1.
cases.note: "your" speaks to someone.

cases.text: Hostile vehicle on Avenue de Paris, about 200 metres from Alpha 2, over.
cases.note: "from" here is a distance, and no pause comes before it.

cases.text: Alpha 1, move to the station and report, Base out.
cases.note: The command post signs off: it is speaking to Alpha 1.

cases.text: Alpha 1 to Base, over.
cases.note: No pause before "Base": the unit calls the command post.

cases.text: Track 2, request eyes on, Charlie 3.
cases.note: "eyes on Charlie 3" could be about Charlie 3, and speech-to-text's commas are not to be trusted. With "request eyes on", the call sign goes first.

cases.text: Request eyes on Track 2, Charlie 3.
Moving to the station now, Bravo 2.
cases.note: the plain sign-off: the call sign is the last thing said

cases.text: request eyes on track 2 alpha 1 over
cases.note: no commas or capitals, a track number right before the call sign, then over Round 1 wanted the unit; with no pause written before the call sign it now waits for the operator.

cases.text: Hostile vehicle bearing 060 300 metres Bravo 2
cases.note: a bearing and a distance right before the call sign, no closing word, no full stop Round 1 wanted the unit; with no pause written before the call sign it now waits for the operator.

cases.text: Track 1 moved to the church, Charlie Three, out.
cases.note: the number as a word, then out

cases.text: At the château now Alpha won over and out
cases.note: won is a sound-alike for one, so near; the closing words are over and out Round 1 wanted the unit; with no pause written before the call sign it now waits for the operator.

cases.text: Two vehicles on Avenue de Paris heading east, Charly 3, standing by.
cases.note: a near spelling of Charlie, then standing by

cases.text: In front of the town hall, all quiet, Alfa 2 listening.
cases.note: Alfa is a known spelling; the closing word is listening

cases.text: Je suis devant l'église, rien à signaler, Alpha un, terminé.
cases.note: French, the number as a French word, then terminé

cases.text: Piste 2 hostile 300 mètres au nord de la gare Charlie trois à vous
cases.note: French with no commas; à vous is a closing word, not a tie word before the call sign Round 1 wanted the unit; with no pause written before the call sign it now waits for the operator.

cases.text: Бачу дві машини біля ратуші Грім кінець зв'язку
cases.note: a personal call sign needs no number; no commas; the closing words are кінець зв'язку Round 1 wanted the unit; with no pause written before the call sign it now waits for the operator.

cases.text: Трек 2 ворожий, рухається на північ по проспекту до станції, від Сокола, прийом.
cases.note: від right before the call sign says it is the sender; it comes after the first eight words, so only the sign-off rule can read it

cases.text: Control, Track 2 is hostile, moving east on Avenue de Paris, Bravo 2 over.
cases.note: opens with the command post's call sign and no sender follows it, so the sign-off is still read

cases.text: Track 2 is hostile, moving north on Avenue de Paris towards the station, this is Charlie 3, over.
cases.note: this is right before the call sign says it is the sender, though is alone is a tie word; it comes after the first eight words

cases.text: Moving to the church with Alpha 2.
cases.note: with ties Alpha 2 into the sentence: it is who the speaker is with, not the sender

cases.text: The unit holding the station is Bravo 2, over.
cases.note: is without this before it is a tie word, not the this is exception

cases.text: 300 metres short of objective Alpha 2, over.
cases.note: objective is a tie word: Alpha 2 with its number is a place here

cases.text: Je suis à la gare avec Bravo 2, terminé.
cases.note: French tie word avec before the call sign

cases.text: Біля церкви, бачу Грома, прийом.
cases.note: Ukrainian tie word бачу: the speaker sees Грім

cases.text: Стою біля вокзалу разом з Соколом.
cases.note: Ukrainian tie word з before the call sign in the instrumental case

cases.text: У церкви две машины, вижу Сокола, приём.
cases.note: Russian tie word вижу before the call sign

cases.text: Holding at phase line Alpha, over.
cases.note: Alpha with no number at the end is not a sign-off, and no tie word is needed to say so

cases.text: Two vehicles moving east past the church, Charlie, out.
cases.note: Charlie alone at the end is not a sign-off, though at the start it would be a near match for CHARLIE 3

cases.text: Track 1 moved to the crossroads at checkpoint Charlie.
cases.note: a NATO word as a place name at the end: checkpoint ties it and no number was said

cases.text: Bravo 2, moving to the station now, Charlie 3, over.
cases.note: the start names a sender, so the call sign at the end is ignored

cases.text: Alpha, at the château, Bravo 2 out.
cases.note: the start gives a question between two units; the start wins and the end does not answer it

cases.text: Delta 4, Track 2 is hostile, Alpha 1 over.
cases.note: the start reads a call sign that is not on the roster; the start wins over a roster call sign at the end

cases.text: Track 2 is hostile, Bravo 2 has eyes on it from the station, over.
cases.note: the call sign is in the middle, not last: later in the message is not the sender

cases.text: Moving to the château, Delta 4 out.
cases.note: a sign-off by a call sign that is not on the roster does not hold

cases.text: At the church, grid 586 101, Alpha 3, over.
cases.note: a clear number that is not on the roster is another unit, not a near match for ALPHA 1 or ALPHA 2

cases.text: Alpha 2 this is Control, confirm Track 1 moved to the station, Control out.
cases.note: the command post is speaking and signs off with its own call sign: no unit reported

cases.text: Leaving the church now, linking up alongside Bravo 2.
cases.note: alongside is not in the tie list, but Bravo 2 is who the speaker joins, not the sender

cases.text: No answer on the net, cannot raise Charlie 3, over.
cases.note: raise is not in the tie list; the speaker cannot reach Charlie 3, so it is not Charlie 3 speaking

cases.text: Hostile vehicle on Avenue de Paris, about 200 metres from Alpha 2, over.
cases.note: from is on the exception list, but here it is a distance from Alpha 2, not a message from Alpha 2

cases.text: Ворожа машина рухається по проспекту в бік вокзалу, двісті метрів на північ від Сокола, прийом.
cases.note: від is on the exception list, but на північ від Сокола is north of Сокіл, not a message from Сокіл

cases.text: Are you still at the church, Bravo 2? Over.
cases.note: the call sign at the end is who is being asked, not who is speaking

cases.text: Alpha 1 move to the station and report, Base out.
cases.note: the command post signs off, so it is the command post speaking to Alpha 1; the start rule alone would name ALPHA 1

cases.text: Moving to the station, Bravo 2. Thank you.
cases.note: speech-to-text often adds Thank you after the last word; an operator would still take Bravo 2 as the sender

cases.text: Moving into sector Charlie 3, over.
cases.note: sector is not in the tie list; Charlie 3 is a map sector here, with its number

cases.text: Correction, Track 2 is friendly, it's Bravo 2, over.
cases.note: it's is not in the tie list; the speaker says what Track 2 is, and did not say who they are

cases.text: Je suis à la gare, je ne vois plus Bravo 2, à vous.
cases.note: French: plus is not in the tie list, but the speaker has lost sight of Bravo 2

cases.text: Holding at the town hall, two vehicles moving north on Avenue de Paris, Alpha 1. Thank you.
cases.note: Comma before the call sign; the 'Thank you' after it is a closing word, and its 'you' comes after the call sign, not before.

cases.text: Track 2 is hostile, bearing 060, 300 metres. Bravo 2, out.
cases.note: A full stop is the pause, then 'out'; 'Track 2' at the start is not a call sign.

cases.text: Request eyes on the station car park, possible hostile vehicle — Alfa two, over.
cases.note: A dash is the pause; 'Alfa two' is a known spelling with a number word.

cases.text: Drone is up above the château; nothing moving on the north side; Charlie Tree.
cases.note: A semicolon is the pause; 'tree' is a sound-alike number, so the match is near.

cases.text: Moving north on Avenue de Paris, about two hundred metres short of the station, this is Alpha 1, over.
cases.note: The pause is before 'this is', which comes too late for the start rules; 'is' here is not a tie word.

cases.text: Two armoured vehicles stopped in front of the church, engines running, from Bravo Two, over.
cases.note: The pause is before 'from', and 'from' is right before the call sign.

cases.text: Базо, ми біля мерії, на площі спокійно, Грім, прийом.
cases.note: Opens with the command post's call sign and no sender after it, so the sign-off is still read; a personal call sign needs no number.

cases.text: En position devant la mairie, deux véhicules sur l'avenue de Paris, Charlie trois, terminé.
cases.note: French: a comma, a French number word, then 'terminé'.

cases.text: Moving up to the church now, right behind the drone team Alpha 2, over.
cases.note: No pause is written right before the call sign, and 'team' is not a tie word, so only rule 4 stops it.

cases.text: Is the drone still up above the station, Alpha 2?
cases.note: A question mark right after the call sign: a question to ALPHA 2, not a sign-off.

cases.text: Can't see you on the square, pop smoke now, Alpha 1.
cases.note: 'you' earlier in the transmission: it speaks to someone.

cases.text: Crossing Avenue de Paris now, linking up with, Bravo 2.
cases.note: A comma after a tie word ('with') does not make a sign-off.

cases.text: Charlie 3, hold at the church until the drone is overhead. Control, out.
cases.note: The start names a unit and the command post signs off after a full stop: the command post is speaking.

cases.text: Two men on foot behind the town hall, heading for the station, Charlie.
cases.note: 'Charlie' with no number at the end is not a sign-off.

cases.text: Alpha, at the town hall, moving to the station now, Alpha 2.
cases.note: The start already asks between two units, so the start wins and the end does not settle it.

cases.text: Are they still at the church? Confirm and move up, Alpha 1.
cases.note: A question mark earlier in the transmission, not next to the call sign.
